body.p: Claims 1-7, 9-17, and 19-20 are pending in the present application. Claims 1, 7, 11 and 17 amended in this paper. Claims 9 and 19 are canceled in this paper. No new claims are added in this paper.
In taking the foregoing actions, Applicant respectfully submits Applicant is not

necessarily conceding in this application that these claims, as originally presented, are not patentable over the references cited by the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO), as pertinent ones of the present claim amendments and cancellations are only for facilitating expeditious prosecution. Applicant respectfully reserves the right to pursue the canceled claims and/or other claims in one or more continuing applications. Request for Continued Examination under 37 C.F.R 4 1.114
Concurrently with this response, Applicant has filed a Request for Continued
Examination with the appropriate fee. Applicant respectfully request that prosecution be reopened and all prior rejections be withdrawn. Priority

Applicant respectfully requests that a claim of priority, to U.S. Nonprovisional Application Serial No. 17/512,421, (App. '421) filed on October 27, 2021, and entitled "TILTING LANDING GEAR SYSTEMS AND METHODS." App '421 claims priority to U.S. Nonprovisional Application Serial No. 16/181,687 (App. '687) filed on November 6, 2018 and entitled "TILTING LANDING GEAR SYSTEMS AND METHODS." App '687 claims priority to U.S. Nonprovisional Application Serial No. 15/198,611 (App. '611) filed on June 30, 2016 and entitled "TILTING LANDING GEAR SYSTEMS AND METHODS." Applicant submits that App. '687 and App. '611 provide adequate support and enablement in the manner provided by 35 U.S.C. 112(a) for the currently presented claims of this application and the Applicant is entitled to the benefit of priority to both applications. Double Patenting

Claims 1-5, 7, 10-15, 17 and 20 stand rejected on the ground of nonstatutory double patenting as being unpatentable over claims 1-3, 6, 8, 11-13, 16 and 18 of U.S. Patent Application No. 17/868,973. The Office alleges that "the copending application recites the use of linked landing gear to adjust the aircraft angle of attack, but does not disclose the gear
mechanically linked, which would be rendered obvious to Dickerman in the manner noted above." (Office Action p.7)

Though Applicant may not necessarily acquiesce to the grounds of this rejection, a Terminal Disclaimer in compliance with 37 CFR 1.321 (c) or 1.321 (d) has been or is being submitted to obviate this nonstatutory double patenting rejection.
Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and withdrawal of all double patenting rejections of the claims. Rejection of claims under 35 U.S.C. & 103
Page/Dickerman

Claims 1-7, 10-17, and 20 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly unpatentable over US Patent Publ. No. 2018/0001999 to Page (hereinafter "Page") in view of US Patent No. 2,469,106 to Dickerman (hereinafter "Dickerman"). Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection.
Claim 1 as amended recites:
A landing gear for a blended wing body aircraft comprising:
at least a nose gear disposed longitudinally forward of a center of gravity of an aircraft by
a first distance and connected to a nose linkage configured to transfer movement
from the at least a nose gear to at least a main gear;
at least a main gear disposed longitudinally aft of the center of gravity of the aircraft by a
second distance and connected to a main linkage configured to transform
movement from the at least a main gear to the at least a nose gear; and
wherein the at least a nose gear and the at least a main gear are linked.
The current application now claims the benefit of priority to the Page reference, as

discussed in greater detail herein above. For this reason, Applicant respectfully submits the Page reference is not prior art to the current application. Applicant respectfully submits that the Office has not asserted that Dickerman discloses, teaches or suggests the Applicant's particularly claimed "blended wing body aircraft." Further, Applicant respectfully submits that none of what Dickerman discloses, teaches, or suggests is any blended wing body aircraft, among other limitations. Accordingly, none of what Dickerman discloses,
teaches or suggests is Applicant's each of particularly claimed system and limitations, as detailed above.

Independent claim 11 recites limitations similar to independent claim 1 and overcomes these rejections for at least the same reasons as discussed above with reference to claim 1. Thus, Applicant submits that claim 11 is also allowable.

Claims 2-7, 10, 12-17, and 20 depend, directly or indirectly, from claims 1 and 11. As noted above, claims 1 and 11 are patentably distinguishable over Dickerman, alone or combination, for at least the reasons discussed above. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that claims 2-7, 10, 12-17, and 20 are also patentably distinguishable over Dickerman, for, at least, their dependency on claims 1 and 11 and the reasons discussed above. Conclusion
Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that all claims in the application are in a

condition for allowance and respectfully solicit the prompt issuance of a Notice of Allowance. If any issues remain, the Examiner is encouraged to call the undersigned practitioner at the number listed below.
Respectfully submitted,
